prompt_boundary.prompt: Import externally produced implementation evidence for the scoped Beacon feature. Read Beacon source of truth and bind the imported evidence to the frozen PRD, user-story, and test-case truth. Implement only against the frozen PRD, user-story, and test-case truth above. Evidence refs: a11685b0c2d4ceeeeaa46ad3021e4cbb8bb37c4f, docs/beacon/v1.4.10/.machine/execution/qa-acceptance-lifecycle-boundary-hook-advisory-and-confirmed-execution.json, docs/beacon/v1.4.10/execution/qa-acceptance-brief-lifecycle-boundary-hook-advisory-and-confirmed-execution.md. items.text: Given a lifecycle boundary such as `post_release`, Beacon discovers enabled project hooks from `docs/beacon/hooks/<hook-id>.md` whose hook code matches the boundary.

Given `release check` passes and an applicable `post_release` hook exists, the release output includes a hook advisory with hook id, plan status, trigger policy, evidence paths, and a recommended confirmed-run command.
Automatic hook advisory may plan hooks and may dry-run no-side-effect checks, but it does not execute side-effect follow-up.
Given a `manual_confirmed` hook is run without `--confirm`, the run is blocked with `manual_confirmation_required` and `side_effect_executed` remains false.
Given the operator runs the recommended command with `--confirm`, the hook executes its restricted follow-up and writes hook evidence.
Hook advisory and hook evidence are marked as support/runtime evidence only and cannot advance or rewrite QA, release, gate, freeze, PRD, user-story, or test-case truth.
Help/status surfaces can show applicable hook advisory and latest hook evidence without presenting hooks as a new lifecycle stage.
Hidden side-effect auto-run attempts fail closed with explicit reason codes.

tasks.title: FR-001 AC-001
tasks.description: Beacon must provide a utility that selects enabled hook contracts for a requested finite hook code.

tasks.title: FR-002 AC-002
tasks.description: `release check` must include a release follow-up advisory when release readiness passes and an applicable `post_release` hook exists.

tasks.title: FR-003 AC-002
tasks.description: The advisory must include hook id, hook code, trigger policy, plan status, blocked state, evidence paths, and a recommended confirmed-run command.

tasks.title: FR-004 AC-003
tasks.description: Automatic planning must not execute side effects and must mark `side_effect_executed` as false.

tasks.title: FR-005 AC-003
tasks.description: Automatic dry-run may write runtime hook evidence only when `dry_run` is true and must not run side-effect follow-up.

tasks.title: FR-006 AC-004
tasks.description: Running a `manual_confirmed` hook without `--confirm` must remain blocked with `manual_confirmation_required`.

tasks.title: FR-007 AC-005
tasks.description: Hook advisory and evidence must be marked `truth_authority: false` and `runtime_evidence_only: true`.

tasks.title: FR-008 AC-006
tasks.description: Help/status surfaces may display hook advisory data but must not expose it as a lifecycle stage or verdict.

tasks.title: FR-009 AC-007
tasks.description: Hidden side-effect auto-run attempts must fail closed with `hidden_auto_run_not_allowed` or `manual_confirmation_required`.

role_semantics.team_reviewer: checks implementation/spec drift before Ralph or QA closure
role_semantics.team_tester: checks implementation evidence and verification readiness before Ralph or QA closure
role_semantics.ralph: post-freeze controller that drives next-action routing across implementation, review, qa, and release

planner.purpose: Compile execution-ready task scope from the frozen revision baseline.

implementation-architect.purpose: Translate frozen requirement truth into implementation-safe module boundaries and service ownership guidance.

implementer.purpose: Write code inside the frozen scope and the implementation architecture note.

reviewer.purpose: Review implementation/spec drift and architecture-boundary drift.

tester.purpose: Check implementation evidence and verification readiness before acceptance.

implementation_preflight: Before implementation, verify the target service belongs to: .
Before implementation, verify the current branch is beacon/v1.4.10.
If a branch switch is needed and the worktree is dirty, stop and clean or stash first.

inputs_contract: conditionally required `prototype` when the feature has real UX/UI handoff
current gate / blocked reason / branch or execution governance context when present
decision_protocol: Enter `implement` only after requirement truth is frozen enough for execution.
Block when frozen truth requires `change`, when cutover guardrails fail, or when a conditionally triggered prototype is still missing.
Keep `implement` as the only execution entry; `ask --execute` and support surfaces may route here but must not replace it.
Prefer explanation and routing logic in skill surface; keep final schema, contract, and gate writes in Python guardrails.
When dual-read or compatibility windows exist, fail closed on mismatch.
anti_inertia_notes: `implement` is not permission to rewrite requirement truth.
`goal`, task ledgers, or partial execution progress do not define completion truth.
If the feature needs UX/UI handoff and prototype is triggered, do not skip straight into coding.
Team/runtime internals stay internal unless the user explicitly asks for them.
`implement` cannot rewrite frozen truth or override gate truth by itself.
learning_notes: Reuse implementation learning to avoid repeated blocked paths or flaky cutovers.
Learning may shape route explanation and caution, but cannot override gate truth.
Downgrade stale learning instead of silently trusting it.
backstop_cli: `beacon qa ...` after implementation evidence is ready
decision_surface.primary_reason: Enter `implement` only after requirement truth is frozen enough for execution.
